summary: Bureau of Reality content policy. policy_lint applies the deterministic rules below; anything it cannot decide is flagged for the judge model and, failing that, for Sahil. A flag is never a silent pass.

reject_categories.why: Finance hosts and advice are a named 2026 enforcement pattern and outside the channel's remit.
patterns: \b(invest|investing|stock tip|buy the dip|crypto|bitcoin|portfolio|returns? of \d+%|get rich|passive income|trading strategy)\b

reject_categories.why: Health advice from a generated character is a liability and a named enforcement pattern.
No real living people. Historical figures are allowed only as part of a sourced fact.
reject_categories.judge: Any proper name not on the cast list that could be a living person.

reject_categories.why: No borrowed IP and no brands.
The Archive covers history mysteries, never crimes against victims as entertainment.
Myth Desk is comparative and interpretive, never devotional.
patterns: \b(pray to|worship|blessings? of|the one true|lord .* will|chant this|miracle cure|sin(ful)? to)\b
reject_categories.judge: Statements that assert a religious claim as true rather than reporting what a tradition says.

reject_categories.why: Adult office satire; kids-coded AI content is the most scrutinised category.
patterns: \b(kids|children|toddler|nursery|bedtime story|abc|learn your colou?rs|baby shark|for little ones|preschool|cocomelon)\b

realistic_scene_disclosure: containsSyntheticMedia is true only when a money shot depicts a realistic scene (photoreal ocean, space, fireworks). Chalk-line animation alone is not realistic altered content.
